visual_events.label: Mason applying and shaping mortar on an edge-laid brick course while a second person walks into the left background
visual_events.description: In a static medium shot, ent_mason bends forward behind ent_brick_wall, where red bricks are laid on edge in two visible courses with hollow cavities between parallel stretcher bricks and cross headers. From 0.0s to about 5.2s, ent_mason uses ent_trowel in his right hand and his bare left hand to place, spread, and trim wet grey ent_mortar along the top edge and vertical joint of a stretcher brick near the right-center of the front wall section. Meanwhile, from about 1.8s to 5.5s, ent_second_worker's legs in light grey trousers walk from behind ent_mason toward screen left in the background, stopping near the left frame edge, with his legs and left hand remaining partly visible near the left margin from 6.8s to 9.6s. At 5.2s to 6.5s, ent_mason reaches his right hand with ent_trowel to ent_mortar_pan on the left, scoops fresh wet ent_mortar onto the trowel blade, and brings it back to the same brick area. From 6.5s to 9.6s, ent_mason deposits the fresh mortar onto the brick edge/joint and shapes and pats it with ent_trowel while steadying the brick and mortar with his left hand; the action is still ongoing when the clip ends at 9.6s.
visual_events.context_result: Mortar is spread and shaped on the top edge and joint of the brick-on-edge course to prepare for or fill the joint, though placement of the next brick is not reached before the clip ends at 9.6s.

visual_events.uncertainty: Whether the mason is bedding a new course or filling/pointing a vertical joint is slightly ambiguous because no additional brick is placed during the 9.6-second window, and the recording cuts off while he is still shaping the mortar.

interpretations.claim: The mason's controlled application of mortar along the narrow top edge and vertical joint with his trowel while cupping his left hand beside the brick illustrates careful mortar placement that helps avoid dropping excess mortar into the adjacent wall cavities.
interpretations.uncertainty: While the mason visibly uses his left hand to guide and contain mortar on the brick edge, some mortar droppings are visible along the base of the wall on the plinth, and the interior of the cavity behind the worked brick is partly occluded.
